name: Density
description: Mass per unit volume of a substance.

name: Celsius to Kelvin Conversion
description: Relation between thermodynamic temperature in Kelvin and Celsius scale.

name: Fahrenheit to Celsius Conversion
description: Conversion formula between Fahrenheit and Celsius scales.

name: Atomic Mass Unit (amu / u)
description: Mass exactly equal to one-twelfth the mass of one carbon-12 atom.

name: Number of Gram Atoms (Moles of Atoms)
latex: \text{Number of Gram Atoms} = \frac{\text{Weight (in grams)}}{\text{Gram Atomic Mass}}
description: Calculates number of moles of atoms present in a given mass.

name: Molecular Mass of A_x B C_y
latex: \text{Molecular Mass}(A_x B C_y) = x \cdot \text{Atomic Mass}(A) + \text{Atomic Mass}(B) + y \cdot \text{Atomic Mass}(C)
description: Sum of atomic masses of the elements present in a molecule.

name: Equivalent Weight of Element
description: Ratio of atomic weight to valency of the element.

name: Equivalent Weight of Common Salt
latex: E_{\text{salt}} = \frac{\text{Formula Weight of Salt}}{\text{Total Charge on Cationic Part}}
description: Equivalent weight of neutral salts like NaCl.

name: Equivalent Weight of Acidic Salt
latex: E_{\text{acidic salt}} = \frac{\text{Formula Weight of Salt}}{\text{Number of Displaceable H Atoms in Salt}}
description: Equivalent weight of salts containing replaceable hydrogen (e.g., NaHCO3, NaHSO4).

name: Equivalent Weight of Acid
latex: E_{\text{acid}} = \frac{\text{Molecular Weight of Acid}}{\text{Basicity (Number of replaceable } \text{H}^+ \text{ ions})}
description: Ratio of molecular weight of acid to its basicity.

name: Equivalent Weight of Base
latex: E_{\text{base}} = \frac{\text{Molecular Weight of Base}}{\text{Acidity (Number of replaceable } \text{OH}^- \text{ ions})}
description: Ratio of molecular weight of base to its acidity.

name: Gram Equivalents
description: Number of gram equivalents of a substance.

name: Molecular Weight from Vapour Density
description: Relates molecular mass of a volatile substance to its vapour density relative to H2.

name: Molecular Formula Ratio (n)
latex: n = \frac{\text{Molecular Formula Weight}}{\text{Empirical Formula Weight}} \implies \text{Molecular Formula} = (\text{Empirical Formula})_n
description: Factor n relating empirical formula to molecular formula (n is a positive integer).

name: Mass Percentage of Element in Compound
latex: \%\text{ of Element} = \frac{\text{Mass of the element in 1 mol compound}}{\text{Molar mass of the compound}} \times 100
description: Percentage composition of an element in a chemical compound.

name: Mass Percentage (w/w %)
description: Mass of solute per 100 units mass of solution.

name: Mole Fraction (\chi)
description: Ratio of moles of a component to total moles in solution. Sum of mole fractions equals 1.

name: Molarity (M)
latex: M = \frac{\text{Number of Moles of Solute}}{\text{Volume of Solution in Litres}} = \frac{w_B \times 1000}{M_B \times V(\text{mL})}
description: Moles of solute per litre of solution (temperature dependent).

name: Molality (m)
latex: m = \frac{\text{Number of Moles of Solute}}{\text{Mass of Solvent in kg}} = \frac{w_B \times 1000}{M_B \times w_A(\text{g})}
description: Moles of solute per kilogram of solvent (independent of temperature).

name: Charge-to-Mass Ratio of Electron (e/m_e)
description: Discovered by J.J. Thomson for cathode ray electrons.

variables.meaning: Magnitude of electron charge (1.6022 x 10^-19 C)

name: Subatomic Particles Fundamental Properties Table
description: Comparison of fundamental subatomic particles.

name: Atomic Number & Mass Number
latex: Z = \text{Number of Protons} = \text{Number of Electrons (in neutral atom)}, \quad A = Z + N
description: Nuclear notation representation _Z^A X where A is mass number and Z is atomic number.

name: Wave Relation (Wavelength, Frequency & Speed)
description: Relates wave velocity, frequency, wavelength, and wave number.

name: Planck's Quantum Theory & Energy of Photon
description: Quantized energy of a single photon (Planck constant h = 6.626 x 10^-34 J s).

name: Einstein's Photoelectric Equation
latex: E = W_0 + K.E._{\max} \implies h\nu = h\nu_0 + \frac{1}{2}m_e v_{\max}^2 = e V_s
description: Relates incident photon energy to work function and kinetic energy of ejected photoelectrons.

name: Bohr's Angular Momentum Quantization
description: Quantization condition of orbital angular momentum in hydrogenic atoms.

name: Bohr's Frequency Rule
description: Frequency of radiation emitted or absorbed during electron transition between two energy states.

name: Radius of Bohr Stationary States
description: Radius of n-th Bohr orbit (Bohr radius a_0 = 52.9 pm = 0.529 A).

name: Energy of Stationary States
description: Total energy of electron in n-th stationary state of a hydrogenic atom.

variables.meaning: Rydberg constant for energy (2.18 x 10^-18 J)

name: Rydberg Formula for Spectral Lines
description: Wave number of emitted photons in hydrogen emission spectrum (R_H = 109677 cm^-1 = 1.09677 x 10^7 m^-1).

name: de Broglie Wavelength
description: Dual wave-particle nature of matter proposed by Louis de Broglie.

name: Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle
description: Fundamental limit on precision of simultaneously measuring position and momentum.

name: Time-Independent Schrödinger Wave Equation
description: Fundamental wave equation of quantum mechanics describing atomic orbital wavefunctions.

name: Azimuthal Quantum Number (l) and Subshells
latex: \begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline l & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 \\ \hline \text{Subshell} & s & p & d & f & g & h \\ \hline \text{Number of Orbitals } (2l+1) & 1 & 3 & 5 & 7 & 9 & 11 \\ \hline \end{array}
description: Relation between azimuthal quantum number l, subshell notation, and orbital degeneracy.

name: Radial, Angular, and Total Nodes
latex: \text{Angular Nodes} = l, \quad \text{Radial Nodes} = n - l - 1, \quad \text{Total Nodes} = (n - l - 1) + l = n - 1
description: Formulas for calculating radial and angular nodal surfaces in atomic orbitals.

name: Aufbau Principle Orbitals Energy Ordering
description: Increasing order of orbital energies based on (n + l) rule.

chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
name: Periodic Table Organization & Blocks
latex: \text{Modern Periodic Law: Properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers } Z.
description: The table comprises 7 horizontal periods and 18 vertical groups across 4 blocks: s-block (Groups 1-2), p-block (Groups 13-18), d-block (Groups 3-12), and f-block (Lanthanides 57-71, Actinides 89-103).

name: Formal Charge (F.C.)
description: Calculates electrical charge difference on an individual atom in a Lewis structure.

variables.meaning: Total number of valence electrons in free atom
Total number of non-bonding (lone pair) electrons

name: Dipole Moment (\mu)
description: Vector product of charge magnitude and distance of separation between opposite charges in Debye (D).

name: Linear Combination of Atomic Orbitals (LCAO)
description: Wavefunction representation of bonding and antibonding molecular orbitals.

name: Bond Order
description: Half the difference between number of electrons in bonding (Nb) and antibonding (Na) orbitals.

variables.meaning: Number of electrons in bonding molecular orbitals
Number of electrons in antibonding molecular orbitals

name: Boyle's Law (Pressure-Volume Relationship)
latex: P \propto \frac{1}{V} \implies P_1 V_1 = P_2 V_2 \quad (\text{at constant } T, n)
description: At constant temperature and moles, pressure of a fixed mass of gas is inversely proportional to its volume.

name: Density Relation from Boyle's Law
description: At constant temperature, density of a gas is directly proportional to its pressure.

name: Charles's Law (Temperature-Volume Relationship)
description: At constant pressure, volume of a fixed mass of gas is directly proportional to absolute temperature.

name: Gay-Lussac's Law (Pressure-Temperature Relationship)
description: At constant volume, pressure of a fixed mass of gas is directly proportional to absolute temperature.

name: Avogadro's Law (Volume-Amount Relationship)
latex: V \propto n \implies V = k_4 n \quad (\text{at constant } T, P)
description: Equal volumes of all gases under the same temperature and pressure contain equal number of molecules.

name: Ideal Gas Equation
description: Combined equation of state for an ideal gas.

variables.meaning: Universal gas constant (8.314 J/mol K = 0.0821 L atm/mol K)

name: Combined Gas Law
description: Relates state variables of a fixed amount of gas between two thermodynamic states.

name: Molar Mass from Gas Density
description: Calculates molar mass of a gas from its density d at pressure P and temperature T.

name: Dalton's Law of Partial Pressures & Aqueous Tension
latex: P_{\text{total}} = \sum P_i = P_1 + P_2 + P_3 + \dots, \quad P_{\text{dry gas}} = P_{\text{total}} - \text{Aqueous Tension}
description: Total pressure of non-reacting gas mixture equals sum of partial pressures of individual gases.

name: Partial Pressure in terms of Mole Fraction
description: Partial pressure of gas component i is product of its mole fraction and total pressure.

name: Kinetic Gas Equation
latex: PV = \frac{1}{3} m N u_{\text{rms}}^2 = \frac{1}{3} M_{\text{total}} u_{\text{rms}}^2
description: Relates macroscopic pressure and volume to microscopic molecular mass and RMS speed.

name: Kinetic Energy of Gas Molecules
description: Average translational kinetic energy per molecule and per mole of an ideal gas.

name: Root Mean Square (RMS) Speed
description: Square root of the average of squared molecular speeds.

name: Average Speed (u_av)
description: Arithmetic mean of molecular speeds.

name: Most Probable Speed (u_mp)
description: Speed possessed by maximum fraction of molecules at temperature T.

name: Ratio & Comparison of Molecular Speeds
latex: u_{\text{rms}} > u_{\text{av}} > u_{\text{mp}}, \quad u_{\text{mp}} : u_{\text{av}} : u_{\text{rms}} = 1 : 1.128 : 1.224 = \sqrt{2} : \sqrt{\frac{8}{\pi}} : \sqrt{3}
description: Order and relative ratio of molecular speeds.

name: Maxwell-Boltzmann Speed Distribution Law
description: Fraction of molecules with speeds between c and c + dc.

variables.meaning: Number of molecules with speed between c and c+dc

name: Graham's Law of Diffusion
description: Rate of diffusion/effusion of a gas is inversely proportional to square root of its density/molar mass.

name: Compressibility Factor (Z)
description: Deviation from ideal behavior: Z < 1 (attractive forces dominate), Z > 1 (repulsive forces dominate).

name: Van der Waals Equation of State
description: Corrects ideal gas equation for intermolecular attractive forces (a) and finite molecular volume (b).

variables.meaning: Van der Waals attraction parameter (atm L^2 / mol^2)
Van der Waals co-volume / effective volume parameter (L/mol)

name: Viscosity & Fluidity
description: Newton's law of viscosity where eta is viscosity coefficient and du/dz is velocity gradient.

variables.meaning: Coefficient of viscosity (Pa s or Poise)

name: First Law of Thermodynamics
description: Conservation of energy for a closed system where q is heat absorbed and w is work done ON the system.

name: Expansion Work & Free Expansion
description: Reversible isothermal work and free expansion into vacuum.

name: Enthalpy and Internal Energy Relation
description: Relates heat change at constant pressure (delta H) to heat change at constant volume (delta U).

variables.meaning: Moles of gaseous products minus moles of gaseous reactants

name: Heat Capacity & Molar Heat Capacity
latex: q = C \Delta T, \quad C_m = \frac{C}{n}, \quad C_p - C_v = R
description: Mayer's relation between heat capacity at constant pressure Cp and constant volume Cv.

name: Enthalpy of Reaction from Formation Enthalpies
description: Hess's law calculation of standard reaction enthalpy from enthalpies of formation.

name: Enthalpy of Reaction from Bond Enthalpies
description: Calculates reaction enthalpy for gaseous reactions using average bond enthalpies.

name: Enthalpy of Solution (Born-Haber Cycle)
description: Sum of lattice enthalpy (endothermic) and hydration enthalpy (exothermic).

name: Entropy Change & Total Entropy
description: Second law criterion for spontaneous processes in an isolated universe.

name: Gibbs Free Energy & Equilibrium Constant Relation
latex: G = H - TS, \quad \Delta_r G^\circ = -RT \ln K = -2.303 RT \log_{10} K
description: Gibbs-Helmholtz relation and fundamental link between standard free energy and equilibrium constant.

name: Equilibrium Constant Expression (K_c)
description: Equilibrium constant for aA + bB <=> cC + dD, and inverse relation for reverse reaction.

name: K_p and K_c Relation
description: Relates pressure-based equilibrium constant Kp to concentration-based Kc.

name: Gibbs Energy & Reaction Quotient Relation
latex: \Delta G = \Delta G^\circ + RT \ln Q, \quad K = e^{-\frac{\Delta G^\circ}{RT}}
description: Spontaneity direction depending on reaction quotient Q relative to equilibrium constant K.

name: pH Definition & Acid-Base Ranges
description: Sørensen pH scale for measuring aqueous hydronium concentration.

name: Autoionization of Water & Conjugate Pairs
description: Relates acid dissociation constant Ka, base dissociation constant Kb, and ionic product Kw.

name: Henderson-Hasselbalch Equation
description: Calculates pH of acidic buffer solutions.

name: Classical vs Electronic Concepts of Redox
latex: \text{Oxidation: Loss of electrons / Increase in O.N.} \quad \text{Reduction: Gain of electrons / Decrease in O.N.}
description: Classical and modern electronic definitions of oxidation and reduction.

name: Normality and Molarity Redox Titration Relations
description: Equivalence condition in volumetric acid-base and redox titrations.

description: Essential chemical compound nomenclature and molecular formulas.

name: Group 1 (Alkali Metals) & Group 2 (Alkaline Earth Metals) Configurations
description: Valence shell electronic configurations of alkali and alkaline earth metals.
